question: Which Indian musician and sitar player is the founder of the National Orchestra of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ravi Shankar was a renowned Indian sitar virtuoso and composer who achieved international fame.
 
• He founded the National Orchestra of India, known as the Vadya Vrinda, in 1952.
 
• Ravi Shankar significantly contributed to popularizing Indian classical music in the Western world, collaborating with many famous artists including George Harrison of The Beatles.
 
• He was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999 for his contributions to music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitar**

 
 
• The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument used in Indian classical music.
 
 
• **National Orchestra of India (Vadya Vrinda)**
 
 
• Founded by Ravi Shankar in 1952, the orchestra aimed to blend Indian classical instruments with Western orchestration techniques.
 
• It was one of the first attempts to create a symphonic orchestra that represented Indian traditional music.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Music**
 
 
• Ravi Shankar collaborated with numerous Western musicians, introducing the sitar and Indian classical music to a global audience.
 
• He performed at major music festivals, including the Monterey Pop Festival and Woodstock.
 
• He also composed music for films, including the soundtrack for the movie "Gandhi" directed by Richard Attenborough.
